2. A dimension obstruction for homogeneous full/dual products

This is the strongest general algebraic conclusion obtained in this turn.

Let
$R_t=\mathbb Q[x_0,\ldots,x_d]_t,
\qquad
H_t=\dim R_t=\binom{t+d}{d},$
and let
$P_{a,b}:R_a\times R_b\longrightarrow R_{a+b}$
be homogeneous polynomial multiplication. Here $d=1$ means binary forms and $d=2$ means ternary forms.

Write $P_{a,b}^{23}$ for the dual obtained by exchanging the right-input and output legs while retaining the left leg.


A finite necessary inequality

Suppose a shared-left border packing computes:


- $F$ full targets $P_{a,b}$;
- $H$ dual targets $P_{a,b}^{23}$;

using $q$ full sources $P_{a,b'}$. Then
$F H_b+H H_{a+b}\le qH_{b'},
\tag{2}$
and
$F H_{a+b}+H H_b\le qH_{a+b'}.
\tag{3}$
The proof is by the two matrix flattenings that separate the right-input and output legs. Polynomial multiplication is concise on both: a nonzero right polynomial cannot annihilate every left polynomial, and products of the prescribed degrees span $R_{a+b}$. Sharing only the left leg leaves the other two legs disjoint, so their flattening ranks add. Linear maps and degenerations cannot increase those ranks.

Consequently, with $m=F+H$,
$\boxed{
\frac mq
\le
\frac{H_{b'}+H_{a+b'}}{H_b+H_{a+b}}.
}
\tag{4}$
This applies to arbitrary linear or border packings with those source and target types, not merely the canonical binary-form gadgets.


Applying it to the required closed round

The second packing in the supplied criterion uses, up to fixed degree shifts,
$a=b'=L',\qquad b=L,
\qquad L'\le \rho L+C.$
As $L\to\infty$, inequality (4) gives
$\frac mq
\le
G_d(\rho),
\qquad
G_d(t)=\frac{(1+2^d)t^d}{1+(1+t)^d}.
\tag{5}$
There is a useful uniform power bound. Weighted arithmetic–geometric mean applied to
$1+(1+t)^d
=
2+\sum_{j=1}^{d}\binom dj t^j$
gives
$1+(1+t)^d
\ge
(1+2^d)t^{d2^{d-1}/(1+2^d)}.$
Therefore
$G_d(t)\le t^{s_d},
\qquad
s_d=\frac{d(1+2^{d-1})}{1+2^d}.
\tag{6}$
The scalar effort exponent satisfies $\kappa\ge d$, already by the output flattening. Substitution into (1) yields
$\boxed{
\frac{3\kappa\log\rho}{2\log(m/q)}
\ge
\frac{3(1+2^d)}{2+2^d}.
}
\tag{7}$

Binary forms | $1$ | $9/4$ | 
Ternary forms | $2$ | $5/2$ | 
Forms in four variables | $3$ | $27/10$ | 
Increasing number of variables | $d\to\infty$ | Approaches $3$ |

4. Keeping the kernel, or adding vector fibers, does not immediately escape

I examined two enlargements that initially look more favorable than scalar ternary multiplication.


Fixed vector-dot fibers

Consider
$T^{(r)}_{a,b}(A,B)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{r}A_\ell B_\ell.$
A calculation using all fiber dimensions can appear to permit better packing ratios.

The actual same-left requirement is stronger: every source receives an unchanged copy of the common left input. That is the condition in the supplied constructive framework. arxiv.org <https://arxiv.org/html/2610.28627v2?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

Restrict that input to
$A=(A_0,0,\ldots,0).$
For full targets, retain only the first right component. For dual targets, retain only the first output component. Every source then becomes
$A_0(\widetilde B_j)_1.$
Consequently, any $m$-for-$q$ full/dual packing of this vector family induces a scalar full/dual packing with the same counts and degree parameters.

The obstruction in (7) therefore survives every fixed fiber rank. Enlarging the dimensions alone does not remove the constraint imposed by the copied left input.


The kernel’s alternating pairing

There is a genuine polynomial pairing
$K_a\times K_b\to R_{a+b-1},
\qquad
F\times G=\langle F,G\rangle(x,y,z).
\tag{14}$
The cross product is parallel to $(x,y,z)$ over the fraction field, and coprimality of the coordinates makes the scalar factor polynomial.

Take
$u=(-y,x,0),\qquad v=(-z,0,x).$
Then
$\langle u,v\rangle=x,\qquad
\langle Au,G\rangle=AG_3.
\tag{15}$
Moreover, $G_3$ ranges exactly over the degree-$b$ part of the ideal $(x,y)$.

For a full target, restricting $G=Bv$ gives $xAB$, from which a coefficient shift recovers $AB$. For a dual target, extending the supplied covector along multiplication by $x$, then restricting the output to the subspace $Bv$, gives the corresponding scalar dual.

Thus any identity-left full/dual packing of the kernel-pair family must satisfy
$\boxed{
m\bigl(D_{b-1}+D_{a+b-2}\bigr)
\le
q\bigl(D_{b'}+D_{a+b'-1}-2\bigr).
}
\tag{16}$
At the required second-round parameters, its asymptotic consequence is again
$\frac mq
\le
\frac{5\rho^2}{1+(1+\rho)^2}
\le \rho^{6/5},$
giving threshold at least $5/2$.
